Refinement of `concepts_sampled_without_replacement` (the incumbent): people do Bayesian concept learning over the same 45 arithmetic and digit rules and every interval of 1-100, with the size-graded rule prior, occasional guessing at their own yes rate, and strong sampling without replacement (each further example a draw from the concept's members not yet shown). The one change, a component taken from `breadth_prior_concepts_free_outlier_rate`, is that how often people believe the program emits a stray random example is inferred from their answers rather than fixed at one in ten. The claim is that a without-replacement learner also discounts a misfitting example as a stray, at a rate of its own, so tight rules and short ranges survive an odd-one-out example (e.g. 85, 19, 91 or 14, 47) instead of giving way to broad concepts.

name: iter4-critique-proxy-stats
description: Iter-4 critique trick — PPC stats can embed a fixed-param Bayesian proxy (stimulus-only, cached) to slice by predicted probability; no iter 0-3 stat was ever significant
metadata:
  type: project
---
Through iter 0-3 no PPC statistic reached p<=0.05. The near-misses were trial-index slope (p=0.05), cell unanimity (p=0.06) and in-set target yes (observed 0.68 vs 0.74). All 5 participants see the same trial order.

Iter 4 (2026-10-30) stats embed `_proxy(df)`: rules+intervals, gamma=0, lambda=0.5, WOR, no lapse. It depends only on the stimuli and is cached in a module dict, so it takes about 1 ms per call. The stats slice by its q: ambiguous band, confident members, late-vs-early false alarms, false-alarm cell overdispersion, single-example correlation. Three new relation stats: digit reversal, double/half, digit-sum.

**How to apply:** reuse the proxy template from iter_4/critique/test_stats; check ppc_results there before re-proposing. See [[iter3-noise-ceiling-wor]].

name: iter4-magnitude-sampling-screens
description: Round 4 cand_0 MAP screens on WOR incumbent (NLL 902.77): magnitude-biased sampling, interval-only evidence weight, rule-vs-range evidence temperature all peak at null
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 4 candidate_0 (2026-10-30). Baseline is concepts_sampled_without_replacement, MAP NLL 902.77.
- Magnitude-biased sampling P(x|h) ∝ x^-β: β=0 is best. β=±0.1 costs 0.4-0.7 nats, β=0.5 costs 18 and β=-0.5 costs 10.
- An evidence exponent on intervals only reaches ρ≈1, gain 0.1.
- A temperature on the rule-vs-interval log-evidence ratio reaches τ≈0.98, no gain.
- Worst set residual: 83,38,58,68 (~20 nats; mid-range targets at 20-40% yes vs 8% predicted). None of the above fixes it.
I submitted `magnitude_biased_example_sampling` (β ~ TruncNormal(0, 0.2) on ±0.6, Chebyshev tabulated, 1.6 ms/grad, smoke loglik -904.7). It may fail the novelty gate if β shrinks to about 0.

**Why:** this confirms [[number-game-ceiling]] and [[iter3-noise-ceiling-wor]].
**How to apply:** don't re-screen these. The screener is at iter_4/candidate_0/scratch/screen.py.

name: iter4-occam-wor
description: Iter-4 cand_5 refinement slot — occam all-concept size prior + without-replacement sampling, smoke loglik -903.5, ~10 min fit
metadata:
  type: project
---
Iter 4, candidate_5 (2026-10-30). Submitted `occam_prior_without_replacement`. **How to apply:** check its ELPD next round before trying more prior×sampling combos. See [[iter3-noise-ceiling-wor]] and [[number-game-ceiling]].

name: iter4-process-screens
description: Round 4 cand_2 MAP screens on WOR incumbent (NLL 902.77) — generative-typicality judgment -40, fixed rule/range arbitration -117, others tie; submitted description_length_rule_cost
metadata:
  type: project
---
Round 4, candidate_2 (2026-10-30). Numpy MAP screens on `concepts_sampled_without_replacement` (NLL 902.77):
- Answering "yes" by the generative probability p(target|D) instead of membership (sigmoid of the log ratio to chance): 943.5. Ruled out.
- A fixed rule-vs-range attention share instead of the Bayesian evidence share: 1020.1. Ruled out. Tempering the evidence ratio: t≈1, a tie.
- Rule share lambda varying with the number of examples: slope ≈0, a tie.
- Description-length complexity cost on the rule prior (lengths 1/2/4): 902.75 with gamma kept. Replacing gamma, it gave 903.45, with RMSE 0.0025 vs equal-prior WOR (close to the novelty gate).

Submitted the gamma-replacing version as `description_length_rule_cost` (smoke loglik -905.2, about 3 s per 200 iterations). The screen scripts are in iter_4/candidate_2/scratch/.

**Why:** at the ceiling, as in [[number-game-ceiling]] and [[iter3-process-screens]].
**How to apply:** don't re-screen these. Evidence-based arbitration between rules and ranges is strongly supported.

name: iter4-sampling-weight-screens
description: Iter-4 cand_1 screens of non-uniform production weights and session drift on the WOR incumbent (NLL 902.77); best +0.56 nats; submitted round_number_salient_sampling
metadata:
  type: project
---
Iter 4, candidate_1 (2026-10-30). MAP screens on concepts_sampled_without_replacement (NLL 902.77). Each changes how the program is believed to emit numbers, with weighted WOR draws.
- Magnitude weight x^-beta: uniform is sharply best (beta ±0.25 costs 2-4 nats).
- Round numbers (multiples of 5) weighted exp(b), with weighted strays: b≈-0.4 gives 902.21.
- Multiples of 10 and single-digit weights: at most +0.3.
- Drift of rule-vs-interval log-odds with trial_index: no gain. The novelty pool also has no trial_index, so trial-dependent models can't pass the novelty gate.

Submitted `round_number_salient_sampling`. It uses Chebyshev tabulation in b (degree 16, error 1e-10), takes about 2 s per 200 iterations, has smoke loglik -904.1 and novelty RMSE 0.011.

**Why:** this confirms [[iter3-noise-ceiling-wor]].
**How to apply:** don't re-screen production-weight variants. Scripts are in iter_4/candidate_1/scratch.

name: iter4-wor-free-outlier
description: Iter-4 cand_3 — WOR incumbent + free outlier rate: MAP outlier 0.124, +1.1 nats in-sample, RMSE 0.010; Chebyshev-in-log(eps) interval tables at 2.4 ms/grad
metadata:
  type: project
---
Iter 4, candidate_3 (2026-10-30): submitted `without_replacement_free_outlier_rate`. It is `concepts_sampled_without_replacement` with a free outlier rate, Beta(2,10). MAP: outlier 0.124, lapse 0.021, gamma -0.10. Observed loglik -901.7 vs the incumbent's -902.9. RMSE of p_yes vs the incumbent is 0.010. Smoke loglik -903.9.

Implementation: rule likelihoods are computed exactly from a (sets, rules, 4) table of member rates. The interval log evidence, and the per-target interval logsumexps, are fitted as degree-20 Chebyshev series in log(eps) over [0.01, 0.45] (error about 1e-12). The "Maximum.make_node" FusionOptimizer ERROR also shows up for the incumbent and is harmless.

**Why:** the outlier rate gains the same ~1 nat under without-replacement sampling as with replacement ([[iter3-free-outlier]]), so the two mechanisms don't overlap.
**How to apply:** don't resubmit this combination. See [[number-game-ceiling]].

name: iter4-wor-free-stray
description: Iter-4 cand_4 — free stray rate on the WOR incumbent gives +1.2 nats MAP (stray≈0.12); in-set-target discount +0.3; exact rules + Chebyshev intervals at 3 ms/grad
metadata:

---
Iter 4, candidate_4 (2026-10-30). I MAP-screened variants of `concepts_sampled_without_replacement`, which has NLL 902.77:
- Free stray rate: 901.56, with stray≈0.12 and lapse falling to ≈0.013.
- Discount on "yes" for targets that are themselves examples: 902.44. These are 50 trials with an observed yes rate of 0.68.

The screener is in iter_4/candidate_4/scratch/s/.

**Why:** consistent with [[iter3-free-outlier]] and [[number-game-ceiling]]: about 1 nat of gain at best.
**How to apply:** don't re-screen these; reuse the Chebyshev template ([[iter3-process-screens]]).

I've replaced the rejected candidate with a different mechanism, and it passes the admission check (`OK`, smoke-fit log-likelihood −904.2). I did not run the novelty check against the live models, which is the gate the first attempt failed.

**Why the first attempt failed:** it added a free stray-example rate to the incumbent. That is the same change candidate 3 submitted this round as `without_replacement_free_outlier_rate`, so their predictions matched almost exactly.

**New model, `shown_examples_not_repeated`:** this refines the incumbent `concepts_sampled_without_replacement` with one change that follows from its own assumption that the program shows distinct numbers. When the target is one of the examples already shown, people sometimes read the question as "would the program produce this again as a new example?" They answer "no", because the program doesn't repeat itself. How often they do this is one new parameter, `repeat_no` (prior Beta(1,6)). It scales down the predicted "yes" for already-shown targets only; every other judgment is the incumbent's.

- **What it targets:** the data have 50 trials where the target was a shown example. People said "yes" to 68% of them, against about 74% predicted. An earlier quick fit of this discount gained only about 0.3 nats, so expect it to tie the incumbent rather than beat it.
- **Novelty risk:** 16 of the 512 stimuli in the novelty pool have a shown example as the target. My rough estimate: with `repeat_no` near 0.08, predictions differ from the incumbent's by about 0.014 overall. That is well above the 0.002 limit, and it stays above it unless the fitted value drops below about 0.01.
- **Speed:** the 200-iteration smoke fit took about 4 seconds, so the full fit should be well inside the 30-minute limit.

I also saved a note on this repair and the duplicate-rejection lesson to the memory directory.

- `hypothesis.md`
- `model_name.txt`
- `candidate.py`
